explanation: Related to erdosproblems.com/982, which notes that the regular polygon shows ⌊n/2⌋ is best possible. This variant proves the bound for concyclic points: from any p_i, each distance is realised by at most two other points of the circle, so there are at least ⌈(n−1)/2⌉ ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ distinct distances. The statement asserts this for every i, with injective points on a common circle (dist to c equal to R), using natural division. It is a correct easy special case (concyclic points are in convex position), with a linked Lean proof. Faithful.
